Comfort Cottages & Bungalows
A world class luxury resort, the Lodge has 12 cottages and 2 forest bungalows
(available for small and big groups) that have been designed keeping in mind the forest habitat and
wildlife. These rooms are carefully crafted in the most authentic sense of style and comfort, as well as
furbished with the modern amenities to suit the needs of a wildlife traveller.
VIEW MORE
A Unique Dinning
At Singinawa, we extend a dining grandeur for our guests. The huge dining area is
located in the centre of the lodge featuring multiple dining options and a bar where our guests are served
with a variety of continental and Indian cuisine, fresh and home cooked food. Lodge kitchen uses the fresh
organic produce from its farms such as fruits and vegetables giving you the ultimate taste of finesse.
GALLERY
Swimming Pool

singing hymns of nature.
GALLERY
Kanha Forest
We take pride in our Sal Stretches, grasslands and waterholes, which serve as a
rendezvous for the denizens of Kanha forest, including large herds of Chital, Wild Pigs, Northern Plains
Langurs, Indian Muntjacs and Jungle Cats. An occasional visit by a Leopard and a Tiger is also not unheard
of. The habitat of Singinawa has also proved to be ideal for several species of birds, and so far over a
100 species of birds have been recorded here.

12 stone & slate cottages are already make for a stand out feature in the
wildlife lodge business. They stand in seclusion and are enveloped with greenery fostering total
privacy wherein the trespassers can only be the occasional wildlings. The rooms are available in
single, twin and double bed options super king beds sized at (80 in × 98 in or 203 cm × 249 cm). They

The Perch
A Four Bedroom Jungle Bungalow
-->
30M2
2 GUEST
1 BED
1 BATH
-->
Perch is perfect for a small group who wants to stay together and for people who are looking for seclusion. The Perch comes with two (double) Master bedrooms, inter-connected with two further respectably sized double bedrooms. All the rooms have En-suite bathrooms; a shared large private lounge-dining room with its own library is situated between the two bedroom wings. Four-room bunglow with living cum dining area; Fireplace with ground sitting in living room; two bedrooms on each side of the living room are interconnected. Bathtub in one of the room (Hoppoe); Backyard opens to the buffer area of the forest; Small kitchenette facility with personal butler; Table tennis room and a small pond outside with golden fishes; Outside sitting with an option bonfire and Khatiyas for sun-bathing Ideal for families and groups. Maximum capacity: 12 PAX with extra bed.
Themed in four different birds such as Indian Pitta, Indian Roller, Hoppoe and Golden Oriole. Living room: Mahua Tree crafted in Dhokra Art by Jaidev Baghel and other Dhokra Art kinck-knacks. Furniture painted in Gond Art. And some antique furniture; Tribal God crafted in Dhokra Art. The Bedrooms here are decorated with bird paintings (Mughal Style) and prints. Dhokra art kick-knacks (such as wall hooks, art pieces etc.) are used along with Gond art painted on the cupboard and windows. Two handcrafted Parsi queen-beds and Rajasthani beds. The outer area has carved, wooden benches along with Khatiyas around the fireplace. We use Copper Water Bottles with RO filtered water instead of plastic bottles and all taps are fitted with water saving devices.

The Wildernest is a two bed-room Jungle bungalow that offers the perfect accommodation for a small family of 4 people travelling together. The rooms come with ensuite bathrooms and a shared large private lounge-dining room is situated between the two bedrooms. The bungalow opens up into an open courtyard with views of the beautiful landscapes. A hand-carved sandstone statue welcomes you at the entrance. Outside in the patio is an Indian Carpet looming machine and Baiga tribal women paintings. The living area is adorned by a Dhodro Banam ( a 'bowed' musical instrument carved out of a single log of wood. It comes from the Santhal community of Central India. The bedrooms are themed after butterflies namely: the Baronet and the Oak Blue; the bedrooms are decorated with embossed cushion covers and photos of the same. The bungalow uses Copper Water Bottles with RO filtered water and all taps are fitted with water saving devices.

Frequently Asked Questions
1. What is Singinawa Jungle Lodge?
Singinawa Jungle Lodge is a luxury wildlife lodge located near Kanha National Park in Madhya Pradesh. The lodge is spread across approximately 100 acres of forest and offers luxury accommodation, guided wildlife safaris, birdwatching, nature walks, wellness experiences, and cultural interactions while promoting conservation and sustainable tourism.
2. Where is Singinawa Jungle Lodge located?
Singinawa Jungle Lodge is situated near the Mukki Gate of Kanha National Park in Madhya Pradesh, India, providing convenient access to safari zones and wildlife experiences.
3. Why should I stay at Singinawa Jungle Lodge instead of other resorts in Kanha?
Singinawa offers more than luxury accommodation. Guests experience professionally guided safaris, birdwatching, nature walks, wellness treatments, conservation initiatives, tribal culture, and the Museum of Life & Art, creating a comprehensive wildlife experience.
4. Is Singinawa Jungle Lodge inside Kanha National Park?
No. The lodge is located outside at close proximity of the protected area, allowing guests to enjoy luxury facilities while accessing the national park through designated safari gates.
5. Which safari gate is nearest to Singinawa?
The Mukki Gate is the nearest safari entrance to Singinawa Jungle Lodge.
6. How far is Singinawa from Mukki Gate?
Singinawa is 13 km from Mukki gate and you will drive for 20 mins through a forest in an open jeep to get there. Getting to the gate itself is one of the experience.
7. What makes Singinawa unique?
Singinawa combines luxury hospitality with conservation, wildlife expertise, cultural heritage, wellness, and one of India's unique Museum of Life & Art, offering a holistic jungle experience.
8. Is Singinawa suitable for international travellers?
Yes. The lodge is designed to welcome guests from around the world, offering luxury accommodation, experienced naturalists, curated wildlife experiences, and personalized hospitality.
9. Is Singinawa an eco-friendly lodge?
Yes. Sustainability and conservation form an important part of the lodge's philosophy through responsible tourism and support for conservation initiatives.
10. Who owns Singinawa Jungle Lodge?
Singinawa jungle lodge is owned by Mrs Tulika Kedia a Holistic educationist and focusing on the areas of indigenous art - culture and wildlife conservation.
11. What types of rooms are available?
Singinawa offers luxury cottages and suites designed to blend with the surrounding forest while providing modern comforts.
12. Do all cottages have forest views?
Yes, all accommodations are designed to offer privacy and views of the surrounding natural landscape.
13. Are the rooms at Singinawa air-conditioned?
Yes.
14. Is Wi-Fi available at Singinawa?
Yes, Wi-Fi is available all throughout the property.
15. Are family rooms available at Singinawa Jungle Lodge?
Yes. Families can choose accommodation suitable for multiple guests. Singinawa has a two room bungalow and a four room bungalow as well.
16. Is the Singinawa Jungle lodge suitable for honeymoon couples?
Yes. The peaceful forest setting makes it ideal for couples seeking privacy and nature.
17. Does the Singinawa Jungle lodge have a swimming pool?
Yes.
18. Does the Singinawa Jungle lodge have a spa?
Yes. Guests can enjoy wellness therapies designed to complement their wildlife holiday.
19. Are pets allowed at Singinawa Jungle Lodge?
No, pets are not allowed.
20. Is room service available?
Yes we do. But given the forest settings and vast expanse, we generally do not recommend room service.
However the 4 bedroom private bungalow ‘Perch’ has an in-house dining room butler service. Also the 2 bedroom bungalow ‘Wildernest’ has an in-house dining room.
21 . Does Singinawa arrange tiger safaris?
Yes. The lodge assists guests in arranging jeep safaris into Kanha National Park subject to permit availability.
22. Can I book safari permits through the Singinawa Jungle lodge?
Yes. Guests are encouraged to request safari bookings well in advance.
23. How many safaris should I book in Kanha?
Wildlife sightings vary. Booking three to five safaris generally improves the chances of observing different wildlife species.
24. Are tiger sightings guaranteed in Kanha?
No. Kanha is a wild ecosystem, and sightings depend on multiple factors.
25. What all animals can I see in Kanha?
Visitors may encounter Bengal Tigers, Leopards, Barasingha, Gaur, Wild Dogs (Dholes), Sloth Bears, Sambar, Chital, Barking Deer, Langurs, Wild Boar, and numerous bird species.
26. Is Kanha good for birdwatching?
Yes. Kanha National Park supports more than 300 recorded bird species, making it one of Central India's premier birdwatching destinations.
27. Can children join safaris?
Yes, for the kids above 5 years of age should have name on the permit and it also depends on the child's comfort during long drives.
28. Can photographers hire exclusive vehicles?
Yes. Exclusive jeep safaris can generally be arranged, subject to permit availability.
29. Which safari zone is best in Kanha?
